reference.title: Smith Behind Neck Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the bottom and brace, breathe out as you press up; breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; the EMG studies used 60-80% of 1RM (Campos 2020; Saeterbakken 2013)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; standing dumbbell press for more deltoid and core demand

cues.text: Sit tall on a bench set under the Smith bar so the bar runs just behind the head; feet planted. Wide overhand grip (hands well outside the shoulders), turn the bar off the pegs and hold it overhead with the arms nearly straight.
Breathe in and lower the bar behind the head, elbows out to the sides and under the bar, head and chin slightly forward so the bar passes clear.
Stop with the bar at about the base of the skull, upper arms about level; do not drop it onto the neck.
Breathe out and press straight up the rails to nearly straight arms.
Hold the top briefly, re-brace, go again; after the last rep turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Lowering the bar onto the neck
mistakes.fix: Stop at the base of the skull; set the safety stops there.

mistakes.mistake: Forcing the range with stiff shoulders
mistakes.fix: Only press behind the neck if the arms reach this position without pain; otherwise press in front.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing the head far forward or arching the back
mistakes.fix: Sit tall, chin slightly tucked, ribs down.

mistakes.mistake: Locking the elbows hard at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop just short of a hard lockout.

kinematics.norm: Wide, hands well outside the shoulders (common coaching)
kinematics.setup: 78 cm between the bar grips (shoulder joints 40.5 cm apart)

kinematics.norm: From about level upper arms at the bottom to overhead (clinical opinion)
kinematics.peak: ≈61° at the bottom (upper arm from hanging)

kinematics.norm: About 90 degrees or more at the bottom to nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Behind the head: fixed by the guide rails: the bar can only travel along them (here a rail line fitted to the free-bar path, a few degrees from vertical at most)
kinematics.setup: Vertical rails 4.4 cm behind the back of the head; top 148.6 cm high
kinematics.peak: Bottom 111 cm high (13 cm above the shoulder joints, the bar 1 cm off the head, neck and traps); 37.6 cm of travel

kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (clinical opinion)
kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s at the bottom, 1.2 s up

sources.title: GymVisual, Smith Behind Neck Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Tsuruike & Ellenbecker 2019, scapular muscle electromyographic activity during abduction exercises in the scapular plane in three positions (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(6):935-944)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
The behind-the-neck position needs a lot of shoulder external rotation; skip it if it pinches, and set the safety stops at the base of the skull.
Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder pain: press in front of the face instead, and stop short of full overhead.
regressions: Smith or machine shoulder press in front of the head.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main shoulder flexor-abductor of the press. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four common upper-body exercises (Campos 2020); dumbbells gave more anterior deltoid activity than a barbell (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main shoulder flexor-abductor of the press. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four common upper-body exercises (Campos 2020); dumbbells gave more anterior deltoid activity than a barbell (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the upper arm out and up. Medial deltoid activity in the press was close to that in the lateral raise (Campos 2020); seated was about 15% lower than standing with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the upper arm out and up. Medial deltoid activity in the press was close to that in the lateral raise (Campos 2020); seated was about 15% lower than standing with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow in the top half of the press.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbow in the top half of the press.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation and protraction of the shoulder blade, so the arm can reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation and protraction of the shoulder blade, so the arm can reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder; much less active than the front and side heads, and lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder; much less active than the front and side heads, and lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred in the socket as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred in the socket as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk still against the pad. Core activity was lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2012).

guides.label: Straight up the rails behind the head
Elbows about 90 degrees at the bottom
